title: Kit Out Beyond the Date Written on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## When the kit is due and when it is overdue

Kit is due back by the shop's closing time on the date written on the agreement.

Kit is flagged as overdue only once the grace period has run out counted in elapsed hours from the time the kit was due back. The grace period is measured in whole elapsed hours on the shop's local clock, counted forward from the shop's closing time on the date the kit was due back; elapsed hours are never mixed with calendar days, and an hour begun is not an hour elapsed. The hour at which the grace period is exactly exhausted is itself inside the test, so the flag stands once that many whole hours have elapsed.

The date the kit was due back is taken from the agreement as the collective's records carry it, and the grace figure is the one held against the package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line the agreement is written on.

### The count on hypothetical hours

Take a package whose grace figure is 2 whole hours, and a shop closing at five in the afternoon on the due date.

| Time the shop looks at the agreement | Whole hours elapsed since closing | Kit flagged overdue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| six in the afternoon | 1 | no |
| ten minutes to seven | 1 | no |
| seven in the evening | 2 | yes |
| eight in the evening | 3 | yes |

The second row is the boundary an hour begun makes: one hour and fifty minutes is one whole hour elapsed, not two.

## Which agreements can carry a fee

A fee is raised against an agreement only while the agreement stands in the confirmed, picked up, overdue, returned, cancelled or uncollected state, that standing being read from the collective's records for the one agreement before the fee is raised. An agreement standing reserved or closed does not carry a fee.

## Clauses no longer in force

The clause reading "From then the package's late fee is raised for each calendar day the kit stays out, counted from the day after the due date through the day it is handed in inclusive, and a day begun is charged as a whole day" is **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which the fee for kit handed in late is worked out.

The clause reading "Once the kit has been out beyond the package's replacement threshold it is treated as not coming back: late fees stop accruing, the package's replacement value is charged instead, and the security hold is applied against it" is likewise no longer in force, superseded by the current basis for kit that has reached a shop counter.

The clause reading "Kit handed in after being charged as a replacement is refunded the replacement value less the late fees that had accrued to the threshold, and the shop, not the desk, decides whether the item is fit to go back into stock" is likewise no longer in force, superseded by the current ceiling on the fee.

Those three sentences alone are withdrawn. Each package of the line keeps the figures held against it: its grace in whole hours, its late fee for each calendar day and the number of days beyond the due date after which kit is treated as not coming back.

superseded_clauses: From then the package's late fee is raised for each calendar day the kit stays out, counted from the day after the due date through the day it is handed in inclusive, and a day begun is charged as a whole day.

Once the kit has been out beyond the package's replacement threshold it is treated as not coming back: late fees stop accruing, the package's replacement value is charged instead, and the security hold is applied against it.

Kit handed in after being charged as a replacement is refunded the replacement value less the late fees that had accrued to the threshold, and the shop, not the desk, decides whether the item is fit to go back into stock.
